newsitem.title: SWEDEN: S-E-Banken says lower credit losses aid H1 profit.
newsitem.headline: S-E-Banken says lower credit losses aid H1 profit.

text.p: Swedish commercial bank S-E-Banken on Tuesday posted a seven percent rise in operating profit for the first half of 1997, saying the improvement was mainly due to a fall in credit losses.
The bank, the first of Sweden's big four to report for the six-month period, posted an operating profit of 2.86 billion crowns, down on market expectations of 3.02 billion crowns.

"This improvement is primarily due to declining lending losses. Total income is growing in spite of the continued pressure on margins," said Jacob Wallenberg, president and group chief executive, in a statement.

The bank said lending losses plummeted by 70 percent to 250 million crowns ($31.2 million), and the lending loss level dropped to 0.18 percent from 0.67 percent a year earlier. Doubtful claims fell 20 percent to 4.81 billion crowns.

S-E-Banken said deposits rose 14 percent from a year ago, and the bank increased its market share to 19.1 percent from 17.8 percent mostly thanks to higher deposits from companies and municipalities in Swedish crowns and foreign currencies.
Shares in the bank, whose full name is Skandinaviska Enskilda Banken, dropped four crowns to 94.5 immediately after the publication of the result. ($ = 8.015 Swedish Crowns)
